name: Turso
tagline: Managed SQLite-compatible cloud for database-per-tenant apps, with embedded replicas and offline sync.
description: Turso is the managed cloud from the company behind libSQL and the Rust rewrite of SQLite now called Turso Database. It hosts SQLite-compatible databases that you reach over HTTP or WebSockets, or sync into an embedded replica inside your application for microsecond local reads and offline writes. Pricing and limits are built for very large numbers of small databases, so per-user or per-tenant databases are the intended pattern, and the free plan includes 100 databases and 5 GB. In 2026 the cloud began previewing MVCC-based concurrent writes from the new engine, which lifts SQLite's classic single-writer bottleneck. It fits mobile, edge and agent workloads well, but not large shared OLTP databases.

pricing.notes: Free: 100 databases, 5 GB storage, 500M rows read and 10M rows written per month, 3 GB sync. Scaler $24.92/month, Pro $416.58/month; overages billed per unit.

scale.notes: Scales by number of databases (database-per-tenant) rather than size of one database; embedded replicas push reads into the app process.

strengths: Cheap to run thousands of databases, ideal for database-per-tenant
Embedded replicas give in-process read latency and offline writes with sync
Native vector search inside SQLite-compatible databases
Point-in-time restore and database branching from a timestamp
Generous free plan and low entry price
weaknesses: Individual databases are small and single-writer outside the concurrent-writes preview
SQLite dialect lacks stored procedures, rich types and roles
Two engines (libSQL and Turso Database) in transition can confuse feature support
Not suited to large shared analytical or OLTP datasets
useCases: Per-user or per-tenant databases for SaaS
Local-first mobile and desktop apps with sync
AI agents that each get an isolated database
notIdealFor: Heavy concurrent writes to a single database
Workloads needing Postgres extensions or stored procedures
